# Introduction {data-gp-section="Introduction"}

* Doctoral candidate at Utrecht University in theoretical philosophy.
* Data-driven philosophy, philosophy *with* AI, complex collective cognition, philosophy of science.
* To follow along: [**maxnoichl.eu/talk**](https://maxnoichl.eu/talk)
* *Towards AI generated Philosophy through Autoformalization*

# Why would we want this?

* Better (AI-assisted) philosophy?
* Understand better how we do philosophy!
* Understanding the differences between AI-generated and human philosophy!
  * Alignment purposes?

# How do we get *good* AI-generated philosophy?

* Out-of-the-box AI-generated philosophy tends to be *cliché/slop/repetitive*...
* AI tends to shine in "verifiable" domains (coding & math), which provide signal for 'hillclimbing'.
* How can we phrase philosophy that way?

# Philosophical theories {layout="half" .gp-dense data-gp-section="Knowledge"}

:::: {.gp-two-col .gp-two-col--side-exhibit}
::: {.gp-half-text}
**What is knowledge?**

* Let's say: **Knowledge = justified true belief (JTB).**
  * As a formula: knows ⇔ true ∧ believes ∧ justified
* Gettier cases: something is wrong with justification alone.
  * Russell's clock: true, believed & justified → *knows*, but we disagree!
* How about: **Knowledge = JTB + no false lemmas.**
* Philosophy, under this view: finding the simplest principles that match our conceptualizations.

:::

  <figcaption>Russell's stopped clock: true and justified, but not knowledge.</figcaption>

# Our workflow {.gp-dense data-gp-section="Workflow"}

1. Research the philosophical landscape: theories & desiderata (OpenAI Deep Research or Codex + database).
2. Evaluate theories on desiderata using independent formalization (Z3). [Heatmap](#){.opens-modal data-modal-type="iframe" data-modal-url="images/heatmap.html" data-modal-navblock="true" data-pdf-click="Stopped clock"}
3. But: "Monster-theories"!
   * Force a simplicity constraint.
4. Pareto frontier: simpler theories that solve more problems. [Pareto](#){.opens-modal data-modal-type="iframe" data-modal-url="images/pareto.html" data-modal-navblock="true" data-modal-pin="Traditional justified true belief"} 
5. Run research flow against the criteria: come up with a theory (verbalized sampling), get feedback, revise. [Workflow](#){.opens-modal data-modal-type="image" data-modal-url="images/workflow_v4.png" data-modal-navblock="true"} 
6. Optimize along the frontier. [Pareto run](#){.opens-modal data-modal-type="iframe" data-modal-url="images/pareto_run.html" data-modal-navblock="true" data-modal-pin="#6 Content-producing"}

::: aside
[@zhangVerbalizedSamplingHow2026]. All runs use a mix of OpenAI's Astra 6.1 & Sol 5.5
:::


# Early results {data-gp-section="Results"}


* For 10 domains (Knowledge, Scientific Explanation, Moral Responsibility, etc.): 26 of 95 literature theories are at the frontier (27% vs. 19% under chance). [Domains](#){.opens-modal data-modal-type="image" data-modal-url="images/pareto_domains.png" data-modal-navblock="true"} 
* Does it work? 
* 52 of 100 AI-proposals make it past the frontier. [Domains run](#){.opens-modal data-modal-type="image" data-modal-url="images/pareto_domains_run.png" data-modal-navblock="true"}
* Some results are interesting, but we still get a lot of "cheating"; literature theories are under-optimized.


# Problems & future work {data-gp-section="Outlook"}

* Lack of "deep creativity" (dependent on landscape → counterexample mining)
* Evaluation is hard (but cf. PhilosophyBench; AI Philosophy Competition)
* No tieback to literature (novelty)
* Understanding our results? Back to essays?
* **Thank you!**
